title: Implement End-of-Day Settlement Batching System over Multiple Sessions
description: The ChromaticLedger system currently processes and settles transactions individually as they occur. To improve efficiency and reduce network overhead, the business requires a new end-of-day (EOD) batch settlement feature. This task involves designing, implementing, and integrating a new settlement module that collects transactions into a batch and processes them upon a specific trigger. The work will be performed over three distinct development sessions, requiring the agent to maintain context and build upon previous work.

project_spec.name: ChromaticLedger
project_spec.description:
ChromaticLedger weaves everyday banking operations into a "color-coded" narrative: each currency, transaction type, and risk class is represented as a hue. Users and demo-visualizers can literally *see* money flow through a spectrum dashboard—blue streams for EUR salary deposits, amber flashes for cross-border FX swaps, red pulses when the fraud-detection engine flags anomalies. Under the hood, a constellation of lightweight C microservices—each named after a color channel—collaborate through an event bus, composing a living, breathing financial kaleidoscope.

Designed for hackathons and teaching labs, the project keeps scope intentionally small (10 source files) while still showcasing serious fintech patterns: a Payment Prism service does multi-currency conversions, a Fraud Hue engine applies rule-based filtering, and a Settlement Canvas reconciles event streams into an immutable ledger. Every event—from a tap-to-pay request to a final settlement confirmation—is stored as a color-tagged entry, letting educators replay or remix financial journeys the same way DJs remix tracks.
dependencies: librdkafka (Kafka C client for event sourcing bus)
